rv.q: She makes an expert witness to fame in all its ridiculousness and peril, who knows that celebrity is "obscurity biding its time."
Confession may be good for the soul, but does it make for good theater? Yes, indeed.
Fisher's material is funny enough, and her delivery appealingly loose and conversational.

Fisher is likable, acerbic, clever and wryly forthcoming about the warped reality of life in the celebrity bubble, but her stage memoir is a journey to self-knowledge that rushes through the bumpiest part of the trip.
The show is a combination stand-up act and slumber party.
